name: Chicken Handi
description: Creamy Pakistani chicken handi with boneless chicken cooked in a concentrated tomato-yogurt masala and finished gently with cream and garam masala.
ingredients: 2 green chilies and fresh coriander, for garnish
method: Heat the oil in a heavy pan over medium heat and cook the chopped onion until softened and lightly golden.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and boneless chicken. Fry for several minutes, turning the pieces, until the chicken loses its raw exterior colour and begins to brown.
Add the blended tomatoes, red chilli, coriander powder and salt. Cook uncovered, stirring regularly, until the tomato mixture reduces and no longer looks raw or watery.
Lower the heat and stir in the smoothly whisked yogurt gradually. Continue cooking until the masala becomes cohesive again and excess yogurt moisture has reduced.
Cover and cook gently until the chicken is fully cooked and tender, adding only a small splash of hot water if the masala becomes too dry before the chicken is done.
Reduce to low heat, stir in the cream and garam masala and warm gently for a few minutes without boiling aggressively.
Taste for seasoning, adjust the final thickness, garnish with green chillies and coriander and serve hot.
tips: Add yogurt over moderate-to-low heat and stir to reduce the chance of splitting.
After adding cream, keep the heat gentle so the sauce remains smooth.
storage: Cool leftover handi promptly and refrigerate covered. Reheat gently until the chicken and sauce are thoroughly hot.
image_alt: Pakistani chicken handi with boneless chicken in a creamy tomato yogurt gravy and green chilli garnish
image_caption: Chicken handi with boneless chicken in a reduced tomato-yogurt masala finished gently with cream.
technique: Handi should be saucy and creamy, but not watery. Reduce the blended tomatoes until their raw moisture is gone, then cook the yogurt back into a cohesive masala before using cream as the final enrichment.
doneness_cues: Blended tomato should reduce from a thin red liquid to a thicker cooked masala.
After yogurt, the gravy should become cohesive again rather than show watery whey.
Boneless chicken pieces should be fully cooked but still juicy.
Cream should make the final sauce smooth and rich without a hard boil.
mistakes: Adding yogurt before the tomato base has reduced.
Pouring in extra water automatically even though tomato and yogurt already contribute moisture.
Boiling cream aggressively and making the sauce split or greasy.
Cooking small boneless pieces for too long after they are done.
substitutions: Boneless thigh stays juicier than breast during sauce reduction, though either can be used with timing adjustments.
Use plain unsweetened yogurt, whisked smooth.
Reduce chilli powder rather than adding sugar if you want a milder handi.
reheating: Warm gently over low heat, stirring the sauce and adding only a small splash of water if chilled gravy is very thick.
serving: Serve with naan, roti or a small portion of plain rice; add fresh coriander and green chilli just before serving.

faqs.question: What is the texture difference between handi and karahi?
faqs.answer: This handi is creamier and more sauce-focused, with yogurt and cream; tomato karahi is more intensely reduced and usually finished without cream.

faqs.question: Why is my handi sauce thin?
faqs.answer: Tomato or yogurt moisture was not reduced enough before the cream stage.

faqs.question: When should cream be added?
faqs.answer: At the end, once chicken is cooked and the tomato-yogurt gravy is already at the desired thickness.
